topics.title: CRM contacts, pipeline and My Work
Support tickets, teams and human handoff
Automation conditions, actions and dry runs

diagrams.title: From business context to a reviewed outcome
diagrams.description: A selected business supplies resources to leads, CRM, content and proposals. Campaign and outreach review feeds the assistant delivery gate before a provider action. Recorded results return to CRM and support.

diagrams.title: Delivery checks happen before admission and provider delivery
diagrams.description: A reviewed request must match business, channel, account and surface. Runtime must be enabled and the assigned assistant must be published, active and ready. Failure blocks or holds work. Queued work is checked again before provider delivery. Setup never automatically replays held items.

diagrams.title: Source approval and current-index readiness
diagrams.description: An uploaded source is reviewed for content and privacy, published, indexed for its current version and selected in an assistant. Retrieval also checks business ownership and surface permissions. Failed review or a stale index prevents it from being treated as ready.

diagrams.title: Import and lost-response recovery
diagrams.description: Select CSV, map fields, validate and submit. A saved import receipt identifies committed work. If a response is lost, reconcile import status and reselect the identical file and mapping rather than starting a competing import. Outcomes distinguish saved, skipped and invalid rows.

diagrams.title: Draft, review, queue and delivery receipts
diagrams.description: Message inputs become a reviewed snapshot. Any input change returns to editing. Delivery checks occur before queue admission and again before the provider. An accepted queue item can become provider accepted, failed, held or uncertain; it is not automatically delivered.

diagrams.title: Campaign and batch isolation
diagrams.description: Campaign A and campaign B each own a channel-specific saved sequence revision. Each reviewed recipient batch captures immutable sequence and template revisions. Later batches load their explicitly selected campaign. Saving a newer revision does not silently rewrite prior enrollments or another campaign.

diagrams.title: Inbound support and human handoff
diagrams.description: An incoming conversation is routed to a ticket. A human takeover pauses AI handling according to the ticket state. Without takeover, assistant and account readiness are still required before a reply. Internal notes stay internal; customer replies pass delivery checks and record their outcome.

diagrams.title: Offer review, delivery and customer response
diagrams.description: A draft passes required approval and delivery checks. Sending can produce sent or delivery unknown. Sent offers may be viewed, accepted, rejected or expire. A replacement supersedes an old version. Configured onboarding after acceptance has its own outcome.

diagrams.title: Active file, Trash and permanent deletion
diagrams.description: Active files can move to Trash after dependency review. Trash retains quota for thirty days and can restore an eligible file. Expiry or separately confirmed permanent deletion leads to purge/object cleanup. Published links are not revoked simply by moving a file to Trash.

diagrams.title: Rule evaluation and execution
diagrams.description: A scoped event is matched against an active rule revision and conditions. A dry run previews actions without execution. Real runs record ordered action steps and outcomes; delivery actions require current account, assistant and provider checks. Uncertain steps require review.

diagrams.title: Reservation, actual usage and original-transaction refund
diagrams.description: A supported task reserves maximum cost with a durable resource. Final actual usage is settled against the original deduction. Unused credits return once to the original organization. An eligible failed operation may refund the original deduction. Transaction activity records each outcome.
